column1: # p14 speculative-decoding spec-type sweep, 2026-08-22.
# QUESTION: generation is the bandwidth-bound path on this box, and speculative decoding is the
# technique that amortises weight reads across tokens. Is the configured --spec-type draft-mtp
# the right choice, and is --spec-draft-n-max 2 leaving tokens on the table?
# FIRST FINDING, measured before this sweep: --spec-draft-n-max IS A NO-OP with draft-mtp.
# Per-request speculative.n_max at 1, 2 and 6 gave draft-tokens-per-output-token of 0.74, 0.77
# and 0.77 -- Qwen3.6's MTP head emits ONE draft token per step regardless. The cap is not the
# binding constraint, so raising it (the unit sets 2, the build defaults to 3) buys nothing.
# Do not bother changing it.
# METHOD: spec-type is a startup flag, so each arm is its own server. Only one large model may
# be resident at a time on this box, so arms run strictly serially with a full teardown between
# them, polling until the process is gone. llama-test.service stopped for the duration and
# restarted at the end; its unit file was NOT modified. Test servers used a scratch prompt-cache
# dir so the live cache was untouched. 3 rounds, 18k cold prompt, 400 generated tokens.
# RESULT -- all 3 rounds, n=3:
#   arm           TG mean   sd     vs none   draft/tok   accept%   PP mean
# CONCLUSION: the configured draft-mtp is already the best of the four, and it is worth +13% TG.
# NOTHING TO CHANGE. The ngram variants are recorded so nobody tries them again: their drafts
# are rejected 87-92% of the time, and ngram-cache is CATASTROPHIC at -32% -- markedly worse
# than no speculation at all, because rejected drafts cost verify work for nothing.
# The trade, stated honestly: draft-mtp costs ~4% of PREFILL (431.2 vs 449.8) to buy +13% of
# generation. Net positive for interactive use, where prefill is mostly cache hits and
# generation is what you watch.
# METHOD CAVEAT: arms ran in fixed order within each round (none, draft-mtp, ngram-cache,
# ngram-map-k) rather than randomised, so position/thermal effects are not fully separated from
# arm effects. The TG gaps are far too large for that to matter; the ~4% PP figure is the one to
# re-measure with randomised order before citing it as exact.
